markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the election results are certified.
markets.rules_primary: If Abdul El-Sayed's margin of victory outperforms that of the Real Clear Polling average at 10 AM ET on Nov 3, 2026 in the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Michigan, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market compares the official certified election result to the specified poll or polling average. "Outperform" means the actual result exceeds the poll figure; "underperform" means it falls short. Only certified results count - not preliminary tallies or projections. If using a poll range, the midpoint is used for comparison. Margins of error are not considered; any difference counts as over/underperformance.

For the purposes of this market, the Real Clear Polling average for the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Michigan at 10 AM ET on November 3, 2026 is used to determine relative performance. At that time the average was El-Sayed 50.3%, Rogers 45.0% (El-Sayed +5.3), so Abdul El-Sayed's polling margin is +5.3 points. Abdul El-Sayed outperforms if the certified margin of victory is greater than +5.3 points.

For a winning candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate's vote share and their closest competitor's share. For a losing candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate’s vote share and the vote share of the candidate immediately ahead of them. Positive margins indicate the candidate won, negative margins indicate they lost, and zero indicates a tie. The polling margin is calculated the same way from the RCP Average figures, so a deficit in the average is a negative margin. Vote shares are percentages of all votes cast for the office.

Write-in votes are aggregated as a single candidate if not individually reported. Only certified results are used for resolution. Certification by the competent authority is the final result, even if later challenged, recounted, or litigated.
markets.title: Will Abdul El-Sayed outperform the Real Clear Polling average in the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Michigan?

markets.rules_primary: If Tre Tucker finishes within the top 5 highest in total full-PPR fantasy points for all WRs in Week 11 of the 2026 Pro Football regular season, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market uses Sleeper's total full-PPR fantasy points for Week 11 of the 2026 Pro Football regular season, including overtime. It ranks all WRs, including eligible players without a listed market. Player-group membership is determined by Sleeper at expiration. If a player does not play in the week they will be considered to have scored 0 points.

Dead-heat rules apply in the event that two or more players are tied at the final qualifying position.

If a tie occurs at the cutoff position, each tied player's contract shall settle at 1/N, where N is the total number of players tied for the remaining qualifying position(s).

Example: In a market for the top 10 fantasy quarterbacks, if two quarterbacks are tied for 10th place, each tied player's contract will settle at $0.50.

Please read the scoring format below. All values are fantasy points under Sleeper’s default full-PPR scoring.

Passing, rushing, and receiving

Passing yards: +0.04 per yard (+1 per 25 yards).
Passing touchdown: +4.
Interception thrown: −1.
Passing two-point conversion: +2.
Rushing yards: +0.1 per yard (+1 per 10 yards).
Rushing touchdown: +6.
Rushing two-point conversion: +2.
Reception: +1.
Receiving yards: +0.1 per yard (+1 per 10 yards).
Receiving touchdown: +6.
Receiving two-point conversion: +2.

Kicking

Field goal made, 0–39 yards: +3.
Field goal made, 40–49 yards: +4.
Field goal made, 50–59 yards: +5.
Field goal made, 60+ yards: +6.
Extra point made: +1.
Field goal missed: −1.
Extra point missed: −1.

Defense and special teams (D/ST)

Defensive touchdown: +6.
Sack: +1.
Interception made: +2.
Defensive fumble recovery: +2.
Forced fumble: +1.
Safety: +2.
Blocked kick: +2.
Special-teams touchdown: +6.
Special-teams forced fumble: +1.
Special-teams fumble recovery: +1.

D/ST points allowed per game

0 points allowed: +10.
1–6 points allowed: +7.
7–13 points allowed: +4.
14–20 points allowed: +1.
21–27 points allowed: 0.
28–34 points allowed: −1.
35+ points allowed: −4.

Individual-player special teams and fumbles
Special-teams touchdown: +6.
Fumble: 0.
Fumble lost: −2.
Fumble-recovery touchdown: +6.

Extra point made: +1.
Field goal missed: −1.
Extra point missed: −1.

Defensive fumble recovery: +2.
